title: Certify an F0 scalar fault witness with exact dirty restoration
body:
The QQ16 producer handoff leaves dirty-helper magnitudes outside its completed-stage error theorem. This audit supplies one exact, restoration-preserving fault witness in the reviewed F0 **common-chart scalar projection**: at literal event 24438 the operands are `(-4T,T)`, so one admissible completed relative ADD defect `8uT` leaves `4uT` maximum final data error. All 480 helpers restore and all eight private outputs remain zero on this witness family. Therefore local relative ADD inequalities and exact restoration alone cannot imply a bound depending only on original data size. The derived necessary reserve for the stated F0 tolerance is `u <= (H/T) 2^(-beta-10)`.

The package pins current main `836b19bfa309ceafbc8ee32a15e8c4b10dde7e11` (priority revision 6), includes the task card, full 52-field response, forward rational checker, separate reverse-adjoint checker and public CLI controls. This closes one precisely scoped scalar implication of [Nick Petalas's PR2965 handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2727#discussioncomment-18975580); it does not contradict that theorem. [Claim and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2727#discussioncomment-18977771).

The physical cutwise gauge binding remains unverified, as do native-child interiors, a particular rounding implementation, actual dirty ranges/grids, physical cost and the F17 consumer. Exact grid-preserving ADDs escape this witness. No selected frontier, source input or shared verifier changes; no physical failure or new kappa claim. README/TASK identify the next native binding and stronger numerical-contract questions. Family decision: narrow and stop.

Validation: registered CPython 3.12.14 replay passes; independent reverse checks cover all 712 suffix coordinates and two prefix rows. Six behavioral groups cover source/receipt corruption, altered cancellation sign/location, tiny relative defects, absolute-error/zero-dirty controls, optimization and a read-only Git-free export. Optimized CPython 3.14.7 tests also pass. Selected baseline/source pins, metadata, committed-byte preflight (15 package/input files) and diff checks pass. Live overlap refreshed across 237 open PRs, 2,440 closed PRs and 1,703 discussion records; canonical main compatibility checked. Full selected replay, physical binding, hosted CI and formal-kernel review are not claimed.

Credit Nick Petalas/PR2965, Ali Romman and the QQ16 team, ywz65/PR2540/2707, Arham Tahir/PR2681, and the native/geometry/supplier lineage retained in the source package, including starship-s, Sagar Thakrar, Ross Richardson and Douglas Colkitt. Prepared by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. The two checking algorithms are by the same assisted author, not independent human review.
